INARA-FAQ-001: Use the throttle on the right: tap the up arrow to go faster and the down arrow to slow down. At zero you stop. To steer, press and hold anywhere on the screen; that spot becomes the center of your joystick. Pull back to raise the nose, push up to dip it, and slide right or left to turn. The arrows at the bottom left turn you in place. On a computer, W and S work the throttle, and the left and right arrow keys turn you in place.
INARA-FAQ-002: Let go of the screen. Turning eases out in about a second. To slow down, tap the throttle down; at zero you coast to a stop. Small drags from the center make small turns; it takes a little practice.
INARA-FAQ-003: Let go and coast. When you stop, you can see everything in front of you. Listen to the scanner while you fly; when the tone rises, that's your cue to let go and take a closer look.
INARA-FAQ-004: They point to the Starship and the gas giants when they're off screen, with the distance to each. Follow one to find your way back.
INARA-FAQ-005: The Sun is the only light out here. Debris is lit on the side facing the Sun and dark behind. Far-off debris fades into the black, and the farther you are from the Sun, the dimmer everything gets.
INARA-FAQ-006: Small fields are too small to see from a distance. You'll only see them when you're nearly on top of them, so you find them by sound, not by sight. Large fields can catch the sunlight from much farther away.
INARA-FAQ-007: No. The debris fields are scattered in a new pattern every time you launch, so there's nothing to memorize. The Sun, Jupiter, Saturn and the Starship always stay where they are.
INARA-FAQ-008: Everything out here drifts. The four rings of debris slowly orbit the Sun, the inner rings faster than the outer ones. If you've locked a field, your autopilot follows it.
INARA-FAQ-009: They're what's left of the four inner planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars. The debris fields are their remains.
INARA-FAQ-010: It sweeps the space in front of your ship. A soft hiss means nothing is there. When you point toward a debris field, a tone rises out of the hiss. It gets higher and clearer the closer you aim and the nearer you get. Dead on target, the hiss falls away.
INARA-FAQ-011: Faraway fields give a weak return, and small fields are faint even up close. Static rides on top of everything, so a faint return flickers in and out. Fly closer and it steadies.
INARA-FAQ-012: Throttle up, press and hold to steer, and look at the rim of your flight stick. A faint gold glow shows which way the nearest field lies, even before you can see or hear it. Turn until the whole rim glows: the field is dead ahead. Then sweep it with the scanner as usual.
INARA-FAQ-013: Your starter scanner hears large fields from about 1,800 meters, medium ones from about 900, small ones from about 300, and tiny ones only from about 200. Tiny fields are the hardest to find.
INARA-FAQ-014: One sweep only tells you which direction a field is in, not where it is. When you point straight at a return, the scanner takes a bearing (you'll hear a soft ping). Move off to one side and sweep it again. Where the two bearings cross, the scanner fixes the field's position.
INARA-FAQ-015: When two bearings cross, the scanner locks the field, plays a two-note chime, and goes quiet. You don't need the hunting tones anymore because you know where it is. A field that's very close and strong can lock from a single bearing.
INARA-FAQ-016: That's fine. The scanner remembers each field's first bearing, so sweeping past a neighbor doesn't erase the one you were working on. Come back to it and sweep again from a new spot.
INARA-FAQ-017: Double-tap anywhere. The autopilot turns you toward the field, speeds up, and slows down as you arrive. You can also double-tap any field or landmark you can see to fly to it.
INARA-FAQ-018: Press and hold. The lock stays, and you can double-tap again to resume.
INARA-FAQ-019: The autopilot parks you just outside the field with your nose pointed at it, so you can see the whole field while you work it. It holds that position even as the field drifts.
INARA-FAQ-020: Double-tap the Starship. Your autopilot lines you up in front of the bow, then flies you in underneath it, past the lit command deck, into the bay. You'll see the guide lights pulse toward the ship to show you the way in.
INARA-FAQ-021: That's the command deck. It looks down over everything below the ship: the planets, and every vessel coming and going. That's where I am when I'm talking you in.
INARA-FAQ-022: Tap the throttle up. You'll launch out from under the bow. Every session starts in your bed, in your Private Quarters. When you go to the Docking Bay, your ship is waiting here, docked in the bay under the bow, ready to launch.
INARA-FAQ-023: You're looking out from its cockpit. Other players' ships will appear once we can all fly together.
INARA-FAQ-024: Once you're docked, tap UNLOAD. Your pieces move across one at a time. Watch the bars: your hold empties as your space aboard the Starship fills. When it's done you'll see TRANSFER COMPLETE and a list of what came aboard.
INARA-FAQ-025: Everyone has their own space in the Starship's cargo hold, and it has a limit. Tap HOLD to see how much you've used. If your space fills up, whatever doesn't fit stays in your ship's hold. The same panel shows how full the whole cargo hold is.
INARA-FAQ-026: What you own is in the Starship's keeping, so every unload gives you a receipt with a code, like WSC-7K3F-92QD. It lists what moved and when. Keep the code: if anything ever looks wrong, the code lets us check exactly what was recorded. Tap SAVE RECEIPT to keep a copy on your device. Every receipt is also kept in the receipts log in your Private Quarters, in the filing cabinet. The Starship's cargo office issues every code, and anyone can check one.
INARA-FAQ-027: Once you're parked in front of a field, tap COLLECT. Pieces drift aboard one at a time, and your ship keeps going until your hold is full or nothing else will fit. Flying off stops collecting.
INARA-FAQ-028: Nothing out here is instant. Each piece has to be drawn in and stowed, and bigger pieces take longer.
INARA-FAQ-029: Each piece shows what it is, its weight, and its size as it comes aboard. Tap HOLD at the top left to see everything you carry.
INARA-FAQ-030: You emptied it. Debris keeps gathering, though: a new field of the same size forms somewhere else in that ring, out of sight. The space never runs dry.
INARA-FAQ-031: Your starter hold is 1.6 meters long, 1.2 meters wide and 1.0 meter high inside. That's 1.92 cubic meters, roughly the trunk of a small car.
INARA-FAQ-032: Your hold fills up by how much room things take, so it's measured in cubic meters. Each material also has a real weight, which is how you can tell what a piece is worth carrying.
INARA-FAQ-033: Gold is one of the densest materials there is: a cubic meter of it weighs about 19.3 tonnes. Here's how the materials compare, per cubic meter: Industrial diamond: about 3.5 tonnes. Copper ore (chalcopyrite): about 4.2 tonnes. Iron ore (hematite): about 5.3 tonnes. Silver ore (acanthite): about 7.3 tonnes. Native gold: about 19.3 tonnes.
INARA-FAQ-034: Every piece has a real size and shape. It has to fit inside your hold, turned whichever way works best. A piece that's longer, wider or taller than your hold can't go in at all.
INARA-FAQ-035: Rocks aren't neat boxes. Each piece takes up the space of the box it would sit in, not just its own volume, because the gaps around an odd shape can't be used. So two pieces whose volumes would fit can still fail to fit together. That room is lost to their shapes.
INARA-FAQ-036: Only pieces small enough to fit in your hold. Every field is a mix of sizes, mostly small fragments with bigger chunks among them, so even a large field has pieces your hold can take. The big chunks stay where they are.
INARA-FAQ-037: Keep searching for a field of smaller debris. Small fields are harder to find, but they often hide the rarer materials.
INARA-FAQ-038: Iron ore, copper ore, silver ore, native gold and industrial diamond. Iron ore is the most common and diamonds are the rarest.
INARA-FAQ-039: Iron ore, copper ore, silver ore, native gold and industrial diamond. Iron ore is the most common and diamonds are the rarest.
INARA-FAQ-040: Small debris fields hold more of the rare finds (silver ore, native gold and industrial diamond) than the large ones. That's what makes them worth the hunt. The smallest, tiny fields are the faintest of all on the scanner.
INARA-FAQ-041: Fields are wreckage, so every field holds a mix: mostly small fragments, with bigger chunks among them. Your hold takes the pieces that fit. The big chunks stay out of reach for now: tools to handle them come later.
INARA-FAQ-042: Tap Exit Private Quarters at the top. You can go to the Starship Library or to the Docking Bay, where your ship waits. The library is open: read its books there or check them out to your bookshelf, take each book's short test (4 of 5 right to pass, and you can try again any time), and design blueprints in its drafting room.
INARA-FAQ-043: From the Market terminal at the desk in your Private Quarters. Pick the ore, choose SELL, and either Sell now (it goes to the best bid straight away) or Set my price (your ask waits in the queue until a buyer meets it). Buying works the same way. Ores trade in lots, and prices are per lot: iron and copper ore in 100 kg lots, silver ore in 10 kg lots, gold and diamond by the kilogram. One lot is the smallest order. Every item has a floor price: nothing trades below it. The Starship bank trades on this market too: it always has a bid and an ask, so you can always sell and always buy. Every trade gives you a receipt, kept in your filing cabinet.
INARA-FAQ-044: Ore, the rock as it's found: iron ore (hematite), copper ore (chalcopyrite), silver ore (acanthite), native gold and industrial diamond. Turning ore into metal is smelting, a skill called Metallurgy that you learn in the library, or you can pay a skilled smelter to do it. About one diamond in a hundred thousand is near-flawless: you'll know the moment you collect it, and it's kept apart in your lockbox.
INARA-FAQ-045: Yes. Every piece you collect is recorded aboard the Starship the moment it's in your hold, so it's still there when you come back, even on another device. What you unload stays in your space in the Starship's cargo hold.
INARA-FAQ-046: At the desk in your Private Quarters, under My items. There's a folder for each place: the Starship's cargo hold (your raw materials), your ship's hold, the hangar, and your quarters, with the filing cabinet (your blueprints, and the lockbox inside it for valuables) and the bookshelf (library books you've checked out).

INARA-STORY-001: You're aboard an exploratory science and research starship, Trainee. Everyone here starts at the bottom.
INARA-STORY-003: She's named for Alexander von Humboldt, an explorer who spent his life learning how nature fits together.
INARA-STORY-004: Fitting that the library's where you start. Learning is how you move up aboard this ship.
INARA-STORY-005: The WSC is the World Space Consortium, the space agency for the whole planet. This ship is theirs.
INARA-STORY-006: It's a civilian agency. That's why our ranks are civilian ones.
INARA-STORY-007: The people who built this ship started with drawings too. Every design aboard began as someone's idea.
INARA-STORY-008: Look back once you're clear. That's the Humboldt, and the lit windows under her bow are my Tower.
INARA-STORY-009: She's parked near the wormhole, past Jupiter, well away from every debris field.
INARA-STORY-010: These rings are what's left of Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, and most of their moons.
INARA-STORY-011: The Sun's still there, and the big gas giants. What destroyed the rest, nobody knows. Everyone aboard has a theory.
INARA-STORY-012: Your first piece. Every bit of ore out here was part of a world once. Treat it well.
INARA-STORY-013: That's your first receipt from the Starship's cargo office. Everything you own aboard is in her keeping.
INARA-STORY-014: That's the prospector's loop done: find, collect, bring it home, sell. Everyone aboard learns it first.
INARA-STORY-015: Job openings arrive in the COMMS at your desk. Read them when you're ready.
INARA-STORY-016: The research labs aboard need crystals like that one. Twenty-six labs, and never enough near-flawless stones.
INARA-STORY-017: Ore into metal. On the new Earth they'll start with stone and clay furnaces. Up here, we have help.
INARA-STORY-018: Our greenhouse sustains itself, and the water plant makes its own water. We never run dry out here.
INARA-STORY-019: Crew Member. Welcome to the crew properly.
INARA-STORY-020: Ninety to a hundred and twenty of us run this ship. Now you're one of them.
INARA-STORY-021: Senior Crew Member. Here's some history for you. The contract to build her was announced on the nineteenth of August, twenty forty.
INARA-STORY-022: Then eighteen years in an orbital yard. She was too big to launch from the ground.
INARA-STORY-023: Specialist. You know your trade now. So did the people who built her: Space Engineering Technologies. SET.
INARA-STORY-024: Some say SET won the contract with influence, not just engineering. That's a rumour, not a fact.
INARA-STORY-025: Senior Specialist. Did you know who christened her? Geoffrey Humboldt, the head of the WSC.
INARA-STORY-026: He pushed for the name. The explorer was his great-great-great-grandfather.
INARA-STORY-027: Junior Officer. Your first officer's rank. Here's a story the officers like.
INARA-STORY-028: History says Alexander von Humboldt had no children. DNA testing found a son. His mother never told him.
INARA-STORY-029: Officer. You've seen what she can do. Antimatter drive, built to go further and faster than anything before her.
INARA-STORY-030: She was built for ten to thirty years without resupply. She was built for a journey like this one.
INARA-STORY-031: Senior Officer. You've hauled a lot of ore. Here's where it's going.
INARA-STORY-032: Through the wormhole is Earth's twin. Air, water, forests, animals, and no people at all. What we recover goes there.
INARA-STORY-033: Chief. A whole department looks to you now.
INARA-STORY-034: We spent twelve months on the far side of that wormhole. We came home to this. The research hasn't stopped since.
INARA-STORY-035: First Officer. One step from the top.
INARA-STORY-036: The rings, the asteroid belt, the moons, and one day the far side of the wormhole. There's a lot of ground ahead.
INARA-STORY-037: Captain. You started as a Trainee, same as everyone. You earned every step.
INARA-STORY-038: I've guided a lot of pilots home from this Tower. It's an honour to call you Captain.
INARA-STORY-039: Whatever comes through that wormhole next, the ship's in good hands.
